confirmed_findings.summary: Detached folder-rename/move DB tails carry no universe-generation guard: a universe switch mid-tail silently indexes the OLD universe's notes into the NEW universe's search.db while leaving the old universe's rows at dead paths.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: rename_folder_db_tail (and move_item_db_tail, line 2782) run as fire-and-forget spawn_blocking tasks that, for a large folder, churn for minutes (measured 19.79 ms/note migrate + reindex each). They snapshot `libs` from universe A at tail start, then re-acquire `state.db.lock()` per batch / per note with no check that the connection still belongs to universe A. `invalidate_search_state` (search.rs:11228) sets db=None on switch and bumps federation_generation, but ONLY the background-attach thread checks that generation — these tails do not. Recipe: rename (or move) an 800-note folder in universe A → command returns instantly (fs final) → switch to universe B; any B-side caller re-readies state.db at B's path → the still-running tail's remaining `migrate_note_db_paths` calls hit B's DB, find no src row (src_exists guard, line 1544) and no-op — so hundreds of A's note_meta/note_links/review_schedule rows stay at dead pre-rename paths (the gated rename suppressed the watcher; boot reconcile is mtime-gated and a rename changes no mtime) — while the reindex loop here calls `reindex_single_note(&search_state, A_path, A_lib_name)` which passes (libs snapshot is A's registry), and index_note inserts each of A's notes as fresh note_meta/notes_fts/note_links/sky rows INTO B's search.db under A's library_name. Both universes' indexes silently corrupted: A serves dead paths in search/backlinks/review, B serves foreign notes it does not own (the exact bleed PJ-235 exists to prevent). No error surfaces anywhere; the per-note diag_log lines report success.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in source: rename_folder_db_tail (libraries.rs:1902) and move_item_db_tail (:2737) are fire-and-forget spawn_blocking tasks (:1730, :2722) that snapshot universe A's library registry once (:1911) and then re-acquire state.db.lock() per 50-note batch (:1935) and per note (reindex_single_note, search.rs:12688) with NO federation_generation check — the generation guard exists only in ensure_search_db_ready (:11537) and the background-attach thread, never in these tails. A mid-tail universe switch (universe.rs:1057 → invalidate_search_state sets db=None; B's first ensure_search_db_ready installs B's connection) hands the tail's remaining iterations B's DB: migrate_note_db_paths silently no-ops on the src_exists guard (:1541-1546) leaving A's rows at dead pre-rename paths, while index_note_impl (search.rs:7884-7888) gates only on file-exists-on-disk with zero library/universe membership validation — A's renamed files exist, so they are fully inserted into B's note_meta/notes_fts/note_links/sky under A's library name, with per-note diag_log lines reporting success. No heal on the B side: reconcile.rs candidates only rows under B's own accessible roots and counts foreign_rows only against federated roots, so A's rows in B's DB are never relocated, removed, or reported (§13 removal is blocked on PJ-224). Timing is reachable: the code's own measurement (19.79 ms/note, ~16 s for 803 notes in the migrate loop alone, :1924-1927) leaves a tens-of-seconds-to-minutes window during which switching universes is a normal one-click action, since the rename IPC already returned. Severity stays HIGH rather than APP-KILLER because the A-side divergence is detected and largely healable on A's next open (MIG-097 cid_cn relocate + PJ-207 drift notice/repair door, subject to the max(10%,200) safety cap) and no .md content is lost — but B's index contamination is durable, silent, and unsurfaced, and A-side rows without a cid_cn fall back to removal, dropping earned link/review data.

confirmed_findings.summary: Successive detached DB tails (and delete_path's inline purge) have no ordering guarantee: a second rename/delete of the same note can run its DB work BEFORE the first rename's tail, stranding a stale index row at an intermediate path or resurrecting a deleted note in the index.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: rename_item returns the moment the fs state is final and detaches its DB tail via spawn_blocking (JoinHandle dropped); std::sync::Mutex on state.db is not fair and the blocking pool runs tasks concurrently, so tails do NOT execute in submission order — especially when the writer lock is held for seconds by another caller (e.g. the unbatched move tail, finding #3). Recipe 1 (rename-rename): rename A→B, immediately rename B→C while tail-1 is parked on the writer lock. If tail-2 acquires first, its migrate B→C finds no row at B (row still at A) and silently no-ops (src_exists, line 1544), and its reindex at C inserts a FRESH row with a default review_schedule; tail-1 then migrates A→B — leaving a stale phantom row at dead path B served in search/backlinks forever, and the note's earned review history/snooze silently reset (the exact loss PJ-140 #16 fixed for moves). Recipe 2 (rename-delete): rename A→B, immediately delete B. delete_path's inline reindex_delete_note(B) runs while the row still sits at A, matches nothing; tail-1 then migrates A→B — resurrecting the deleted note as a live index row at B: it reappears in search, quick switcher and link suggestions pointing at a file that is gone. Nothing errors; every log line reports success. The watcher is suppressed for all involved paths, so nothing heals it in-session.
confirmed_findings.reason: Every load-bearing claim checks out in the source. (1) No ordering guarantee: rename_item (libraries.rs:1820) and move_item (:2722) detach their DB tails via spawn_blocking with the JoinHandle dropped; SearchState.db is a std::sync::Mutex (search.rs:1342 — lock().map_err proves std, which is unfair/non-FIFO), so two parked tails acquire in arbitrary order. (2) The silent no-op is real: migrate_note_db_paths returns silently (no log) when no row exists at old_path (libraries.rs:1541-1546, the PJ-149 src_exists guard). (3) The phantom is never self-healed: index_note_impl returns Skipped for a missing file (search.rs:7886-7888), so tail-1's late reindex at B leaves the just-migrated row at dead path B; the late migrate is DB-only, producing no fs event, and the gated ops suppressed the watcher — nothing heals in-session. (4) The multi-second park window is real and code-documented: move_item_db_tail holds the writer lock ONCE across migrate_note_db_paths for EVERY descendant (libraries.rs:2764-2770, unbatched — the code's own sibling comment measures 19.79 ms/note, ~16 s for 803 notes), and the §B2-4 comments record Boss-reproduced multi-second parks. Concrete recipe: move a large folder (writer held for tens of seconds) → rename A→B (tail-1 parks) → within the hold, rename B→C or delete B (second contender parks) → on release the unfair mutex lets the second contender win: tail-2's migrate(B→C) finds no row at B and silently no-ops, its reindex at C writes a FRESH row with a default review_schedule (the exact earned-history reset PJ-140 #16 fixed for moves — reintroduced by ordering); tail-1 then migrates A→B, stranding a live phantom row at dead path B served by search/backlinks. Recipe 2: delete_path's inline exact-path purge (libraries.rs:8546-8554, reindex_delete_note is exact-path per its own PJ-140 #3 comment) matches nothing while the row sits at A; tail-1 then resurrects the deleted note at B. Every log line reports success; the earned review data lost lives ONLY in search.db (no disk layer). No guard, gate, or reconcile serializes the tails — the gate_rmw path locks cover only the fs section and are released before the tails run.

confirmed_findings.summary: preserveWorkBeforeVacating filters affected tabs on isNoteDirty() only and never asks hasUnsavedRecovery(), so a restore-seeded recovery model (clean by Gate #8, netUnsaved=true) is invisible to the vacate flush; the function returns true ('safe to destroy recovery state') and deleteWithSetting/moveToTrash then run clearPathKeyedAuxStateOnDelete(path) — wiping the write-ahead net that is the ONLY copy of the failed-save work — plus clearSaveFailure(path) and releaseTabsForVacatedPath→closeNoteModel. noteModel.ts:661-672's own contract says every site arbitrating 'is there work here disk does not have' must ask hasUnsavedRecovery; the sweep fixed store.ts:1145, 1350, 4892 and NoteEditor.svelte:427 and missed this one. Note also there is NO flush machinery that could persist such a model even if the filter caught it: flushOutgoing (store.ts:690) and flushIfDirty (noteSession.ts:299) both gate on isDirty and no-op for a clean netUnsaved model.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: A note's save fails (OneDrive/AV lock) → its work survives only in the write-ahead net → app restarts → MIG-100 restore seeds the tab clean with netUnsaved=true (store.ts:3821), net preserved. The user then deletes that note (or a create/rename collision dialog's Overwrite displaces it): preserveWorkBeforeVacating finds zero dirty tabs → returns true → the file moves to .trash holding the PRE-EDIT bytes, the net entry (the only copy of the recovered paragraph) is erased by clearPathKeyedAuxStateOnDelete, the model is disposed, and clearSaveFailure removes the banner. No error anywhere; restoring from .trash returns the pre-edit version — exactly the 2026-08-02 audit's app-killer shape, re-entered through the netUnsaved door that flag cannot see.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in code: preserveWorkBeforeVacating (store.ts:5190) filters affected tabs on isNoteDirty() only; a MIG-100 restore-seeded recovery model is born clean with netUnsaved=true (store.ts:3821 -> noteModel.setDiskBaseline:505-516), so it is invisible to the vacate flush and the function returns true. deleteWithSetting (5104-5107) and moveToTrash (5288-5291) then run clearPathKeyedAuxStateOnDelete, whose walker (store.ts:773-829) deletes the write-ahead entry from BOTH the in-memory writeAheadBuffer and the localStorage constellation-wab backup — the net's only two homes; there is no Rust/disk-side copy. releaseTabsForVacatedPath -> closeNoteModel (5252) disposes the last in-memory copy, and the .trash file holds the pre-edit bytes. noteModel.ts:661-672's own contract requires hasUnsavedRecovery at every such arbitration site; the sweep fixed store.ts:1145/1350/4892 and NoteEditor.svelte:427 and missed 5190. No rescue path exists: flushOutgoing (store.ts:690) and flushIfDirty (noteSession.ts:299) both no-op ok:true on a clean model, netUnsaved is cleared only by a durable write (noteModel.ts:646) that nothing schedules for a clean model, so the window is indefinite. Fully silent: preserved=true skips even the dev-only console.warn, clearSaveFailure removes the banner, and none of the four displacement callers (+layout.svelte:4749/7220/7241/7298) consult hasUnsavedRecovery. Recovering from .trash returns the pre-edit version — silent, unrecoverable loss of the only copy of the user's work under an explicit recoverable-delete promise.

confirmed_findings.summary: reloadTabsFromDisk matches the cascade's rewritten paths against open tabs with RAW exact string equality (`t.path === fp` at :1106, `byPath.get(t.path)` at :1139/:1160) — no normPath, no case fold, no NFC — while the same function normalizes for the Focus surface (focusPathAmong :1076) and its sibling adoptExternalChangeIntoTabs was explicitly fixed on 2026-08-01 for exactly this half-normalization class (:1294-1298, :1332-1338 'made every Windows tab miss, silently disabling the whole arbitration'). The walker's result.rewritten mixes index-row strings (note_links.source_path via cascade_candidates_via_index) with disk-walk PathBuf strings, and Rust itself must lowercase+forward-slash to dedup them (libraries.rs:6922) because the two forms differ for one file; the frontend PJ-092 belt NFC-normalizes for the same reason (+layout.svelte:7491-7499 — 'a leak that reaches here differs by NFC/NFD, the exact Arabic-root form'). So a rewritten referrer whose open tab carries a different case/NFC/separator form is silently skipped by the post-cascade reload.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Note B (a referrer of A) is open in a tab whose path string differs from the walker's returned form — e.g. an Arabic folder segment in NFD in the tab (opened from a search hit / older index row) vs NFC from the disk walk, or a case difference between note_meta.path and the tree path. User renames A → A2. The walker rewrites B.md on disk ([[A]]→[[A2]]) and returns it in result.rewritten; reloadTabsFromDisk (called at +layout.svelte:7509 AND by the defence-in-depth cascade:rewrote listener at :3796 — same function, same miss) finds no tab with `t.path === fp`, so B's tab is never reloaded: the screen keeps showing [[A]] (on-screen ≠ disk, undetectable), the clean model keeps the pre-rewrite body, and the cascade's fs::write was watcher-suppressed so no other channel adopts it. The next time the user types one character in B, the debounced save composes the pre-rewrite body and durably writes it — silently reverting the cascade's rewrite; [[A]] now names a title that no longer exists. No error, no conflict, no journal marker fires anywhere in the chain.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in code: reloadTabsFromDisk matches cascade-rewritten paths to open tabs by RAW string equality (store.ts:1106 `t.path === fp`; :1139/:1160 byPath keyed by raw t.path) with no normPath/case/NFC folding, while the same function normalizes for Focus (:1076) and every sibling comparison site between the same two path populations was already fixed for this exact class: adoptExternalChangeIntoTabs (:1294-1338, 2026-08-01 fix, "made every Windows tab miss… the next keystroke's save overwrote the external edit"), the PJ-092 belt (+layout.svelte:7495, NFC-folds tab paths vs result.rewritten because "a leak that reaches here differs by NFC/NFD, the exact Arabic-root form"), the tab-dedup fix (store.ts:3261 "a mixed-separator stored path"), and Rust's own dedup (libraries.rs:6922 lowercase+forward-slash to unify index-row strings with disk-walk PathBufs for one file). Tabs store the opener's raw form (store.ts:3491) and rewritten paths carry to_string_lossy of index-row-or-walk forms (libraries.rs:7325), so the divergent state is reachable and first-party attested. No healing channel: the cascade:rewrote listener (:3796) calls the same raw-equality function; gate_rmw writes are watcher-suppressed by design (write_gate.rs:256-257, watcher.rs:119, universe.rs:2647); a leaked event is skipped by isCascading (store.ts:1340); the save path does no disk arbitration. The miss is fully silent (filtered with no log; model clean so no conflict; orchestrator inspects only refusedDirty/failed), leaving on-screen ≠ disk and the next debounced save durably reverting the cascade's rewrite. Not APP-KILLER — no user-authored content is lost and the rename-stamped alias keeps the stale [[old-name]] resolving (textual staleness/ambiguity, not hard breakage) — but a real, silent, reachable divergence-and-reversion of app-authored canonical disk content: HIGH.

confirmed_findings.summary: Closed-note tag add reports success while composeUpdatedContent silently drops the edit: on unparseable YAML the H1 branch re-emits the original frontmatter verbatim (the write is byte-identical), and on a block-shaped `tags:` key the immutableBlockKeys filter removes the key from both diff sides so no op is ever emitted. writeNote succeeds, reindexNote runs, addTagToNote returns true; the 2026-08-01 visible-error work covers only the identity refusal / cascade gate / failed-write exits — not a successful write that carried no change. frontmatterIsRewritable exists exactly for this but is called only from the open-note model path (noteModel.ts:163), never from this closed-note RMW.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: A note is closed and its frontmatter has a duplicate key (two `tags:` lines — the yaml library errors with 'Map keys must be unique') or an indentation typo. User right-clicks it in the file tree → Add tag (or runs the multi-select batch tag add, +layout.svelte:10386). parseFrontmatter falls back to the line scanner; addTagToProps adds the tag; composeFrontmatter hits doc.errors and returns the original bytes + body; writeNote writes the unchanged file and succeeds; addTagToNote returns true, so the batch reports the note as tagged and no action-notice bar appears. The tag exists nowhere — not on disk, not in note_meta/FTS — and nothing anywhere reports a discrepancy.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified by reading the full chain. The closed-note branch of addTagToNote (+layout.svelte:7084-7094) does readNote → parseFrontmatter → addTagToProps → composeUpdatedContent → writeNote → reindexNote → return true, with no frontmatterIsRewritable check (grep confirms its only call site is noteModel.ts:163, the open-note path). Mechanism 1: on unparseable YAML (e.g. duplicate tags: key), classifyFrontmatterValues returns an empty map (yamlDoc.ts:114) so parseFrontmatter's line-scanner fallback projects an editable list; composeFrontmatter then hits the H1 gate (yamlDoc.ts:464) and re-emits the original frontmatter bytes verbatim — the tag is discarded, writeNote succeeds on the unchanged bytes, and true is returned. Mechanism 2: a block-shaped tags: key (seq-of-maps/nested map/block scalar) is classified 'block'; addTagToProps still matches it (line 7027) and produces a changed row, but immutableBlockKeys (yamlDoc.ts:502-508) filters 'tags' from BOTH sides of the compose diff, so no op is emitted, the write is byte-identical, and true is returned. The 2026-08-01 visible-error work covers only the identity refusal, the cascade gate, and a thrown write error — neither scenario throws. The batch caller (10386) treats true as success; the single right-click path (10395) is fire-and-forget; markRecentWrite suppresses the watcher for the no-op write. The tag exists nowhere (disk, note_meta, FTS) and nothing reports it. Not APP-KILLER: no existing content is lost or corrupted (H1 passthrough and the immutable-key filter both preserve bytes correctly) — the defect is a silently dropped user action reported as success.

confirmed_findings.summary: addLinkToNote's CLOSED branch has the same silent drop as the closed tag add: composeUpdatedContent H1-passthroughs the typed-link property when the target note's YAML does not parse (or the immutable-key filter drops it when the link-type key is block-shaped), the byte-identical writeNote succeeds, the background reindex of the unchanged file derives no note_links row, and the caller — the Reviewer connect, which 'updates optimistically (refreshAfterConnect)' — shows the link as created. The OPEN branch was fixed (PJ-207 §15: saveTabContent's editNoteProps refusal → reportSaveFailure banner); the closed branch never got the equivalent frontmatterIsRewritable gate.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: User connects note A to closed note B from the Reviewer (a de-orphan connect writes the wikilink into the closed candidate's frontmatter). The candidate's frontmatter has a duplicate key or bad indent. composeUpdatedContent returns the original content unchanged; writeNote succeeds; reindexNote re-reads the unchanged file so no note_links edge and no incoming_count bump ever exist; the Reviewer's optimistic UI shows the connection until its next refresh, then the orphan silently reappears. No error is surfaced at any point — the reindex catch logs to a console the release build does not have.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in source. addLinkToNote's CLOSED branch (store.ts:1544-1570) is readNote → addTypedLinkToProps → composeUpdatedContent → writeNote → fire-and-forget reindexNote, with no frontmatterIsRewritable gate, no try/catch, and no notice bar. Two confirmed silent-drop mechanisms in composeFrontmatter (yamlDoc.ts): (1) H1 passthrough at line 464 — on YAML parse errors (duplicate key, bad indent) it returns the ORIGINAL frontmatter bytes verbatim, so the just-added typed-link property never reaches disk while writeNote succeeds; (2) the immutableBlockKeys filter at lines 502-508 — a block-shaped link-type key (seq-of-maps / block scalar) is stripped from both diff maps, so the addition produces no diff. addTypedLinkToProps returns non-null on any fresh connect, so the path always reaches the write. The caller RelatedCandidates.choose (lines 145-152) awaits without error, optimistically removes the candidate and fires onConnected — the UI affirms the connect; reindexNote re-reads the unchanged file so no note_links row or incoming_count bump ever exists, and its .catch logs to a console disabled in release builds. The orphan silently reappears on the next refresh. The asymmetry is real: the OPEN branch's saveTabContent → editNoteProps refusal raises reportSaveFailure ("frontmatter could not be read — fix the YAML", store.ts:1814-1824, PJ-207 §15), and the comment there even names addLinkToNote — but only the OPEN branch reaches it. The CLOSED branch is the common case for a Reviewer de-orphan connect (the candidate is a library suggestion, not an open tab). Fully reachable, fully silent false-success on the Living Link birth act. Not APP-KILLER: the note itself is byte-preserved (no content loss/corruption); the loss is the user's connect action reported as done.

confirmed_findings.summary: libraries.json load→mutate→save has NO serialization lock: retarget_registered_libraries runs on Tokio workers (async rename_item:1712, move_item:2710, delete_item:8528 tails) while add_library/remove_library/set_library_canonical_mode (sync, lines 828/877/864) RMW the same file from the IPC dispatch thread — the losing writer's changes are silently reverted while both operations return Ok. review.rs added PULSE_LOCK for exactly this class on review-pulse.json; save_libraries (line 476) has no equivalent.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: User renames (or moves/deletes) a folder that contains a registered library; the async DB tail calls retarget_registered_libraries, which try_load_libraries → rewrites the nested library's path → save_libraries. In the same window (sidebar or second screen) the user adds a library: add_library's try_load_libraries (line 828) reads the PRE-retarget file, the retarget's save_libraries commits, then add_library's save_libraries commits the stale list plus the new entry. The retargeted library's registration now points at the pre-rename dead path forever: it vanishes from the sidebar tree, from search attribution, and from every resolver, with no error anywhere (the retarget believes it saved; add_library believes it saved). The reverse interleaving silently drops the just-added library registration instead. Both atomic_write calls succeed — atomicity per-write does not protect the read-modify-write cycle.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in code: save_libraries (libraries.rs:476) is per-write atomic but no lock serializes the load-mutate-save cycle; the only mutex (LIBRARIES_CACHE:181) guards the read cache only. retarget_registered_libraries (612) runs inline in three async commands (rename_item:1712, move_item:2710, delete_path:8528) on Tokio worker threads, while add_library:828/853, set_library_canonical_mode:864/867 and remove_library:877/885 are sync commands doing the same unguarded RMW on the IPC dispatch thread — genuinely concurrent. Interleaved reads before either save produce a lost update: e.g. add_library's save, built from a pre-retarget snapshot, reverts the carried library to its dead pre-rename path; both atomic writes succeed, both commands return Ok, the retarget logs success, and nothing reconciles libraries.json (the code's own comments at 599-602 say a dead-path registration silently vanishes from every list/tree/resolver until manually re-registered). The reverse interleaving silently drops the just-added registration. The codebase itself classified this exact class as lock-worthy — review.rs:723-728 added PULSE_LOCK for the identical async-RMW lost-write on review-pulse.json — and libraries.json has no equivalent. Not APP-KILLER because the window is milliseconds wide, needs two near-simultaneous user actions (second screen / racing clicks), and the .md files are untouched — the loss is a registry entry, hand-recoverable once noticed; but it is a silent, permanent-until-fixed divergence of a source-of-truth JSON with false success on both sides: HIGH.

confirmed_findings.summary: run_one_safe's per-cataloger timeout is structurally inert: the worker runs under std::thread::scope, which JOINS all spawned threads before returning, so after rx.recv_timeout fires the function still blocks until c.classify() actually finishes. The V3-§8.r4.4 comment claims the exact opposite ('recv_timeout enforces the per-cataloger budget'), making this a false guard the codebase believes exists.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: A background writer (index repair, backfill, migration) holds the SQLite writer lock while the Semantic cataloger classifies a note: wiring.rs::knn_classified_neighbors → with_read_conn falls back to the WRITER lock when the dedicated reader is absent, and the cataloger thread parks on it. recv_timeout(2s) fires, an abstain trail is built — then std::thread::scope blocks anyway until the lock frees, which can be indefinitely. Consequences, all silent: (a) 'Classify open note' — the awaited invoke never resolves, spinner stuck forever, no error; (b) on_save auto-classify — the promise silently never settles; (c) classifier_scan_start — run_scan wedges mid-note, ScanState.running stays true permanently, cancel is only checked BETWEEN notes so it is ineffective, no error event fires, and every subsequent scan attempt returns 'Scan already running' until app restart. Secondary defect on the non-hang path: a cataloger finishing at timeout+ε has its valid verdict discarded (replaced by abstain) while its full cost is still paid.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in code: run_one_safe (orchestrator.rs:153) spawns the cataloger via scope.spawn inside std::thread::scope, which by Rust language guarantee joins all spawned threads before returning — so after rx.recv_timeout(2s/5s/500ms) fires and the abstain trail is built, the function still blocks until c.classify() actually finishes. The V3-§8.r4.4 comment (lines 130-136) claims recv_timeout "enforces the per-cataloger budget" and was added specifically to fix audit P1.4 (hangs blocking the IPC indefinitely); the fix isolates panics but is structurally inert against hangs — a false guard the codebase documents as real. Reachable long blocks confirmed at the sites the candidate names: (1) knn_classified_neighbors (wiring.rs:149) calls ensure_search_db_ready inside classify — documented 20-40s cold init (scan_job.rs:110-115); (2) with_read_conn (search.rs:1492) falls back to the writer Mutex when the reader is absent, a real state (read_db open failure at search.rs:11631 falls back permanently; universe-switch clears it at 11268), and index_repair.rs:175 documents the defrag worker holding state.db for its VACUUM — an unbounded Mutex park; (3) the r4.4 comment's own premise, catastrophic regex backtracking in Structural. Consequences verified: run_scan (scan_job.rs:188-238) checks cancel only BETWEEN notes, running resets only when the worker returns (line 151), so a mid-note wedge makes cancel ineffective and every subsequent start returns "Scan already running" (line 123) until restart; the on-demand IPC promise never settles. All silent — only eprintln to stderr, invisible in release builds. Secondary defect also verified: a cataloger finishing after timeout has its valid verdict discarded via the ignored tx.send while its full cost is still paid. Not APP-KILLER: no source-of-truth loss/corruption, and the guaranteed-indefinite variant needs a conjunction (reader absent + long writer hold, or pathological regex); steady-state blocks are bounded (reader busy_timeout 5s, local ONNX embed, ~155ms warm kNN).

confirmed_findings.summary: Backfill worker threads carry NO universe-generation guard (grep: zero 'generation' matches in any *backfill*.rs, vs the capture/re-check pattern in the federation attach thread and WAL daemon). A worker that survives a universe switch A->B — reachable because invalidate_search_state only sets db=None and the worker re-locks state.db per batch, so a switch whose re-init completes inside the worker's off-lock window (sky_backfill's off-lock .md reads, or the 50ms inter-batch sleep) hands it universe B's connection — keeps writing with universe A's thread-local state. review_backfill is the sharpest instance: cdir (A's .constellation, hence A's review-pulse.json) is pinned at run() line 72 and last_path holds A's cursor, so process_batch (line 78) builds B's review_schedule rows from A's pulse data, skips every B note sorting <= A's cursor, then finalize (line 80) stamps schema_versions.review complete. Same unguarded shape in sky_backfill.rs run() 102-161 (finalize stamps sky with the range below A's cursor never populated — Sky View reads stored rows, never re-walks), links_backfill.rs (stamps A's vocab fingerprint into B), note_body_backfill.rs, and siblings.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Universe A (7,600+ notes) is mid review-backfill at cursor 'M...'; the user switches to unstamped universe B; ensure_search_db_ready publishes B's connection while A's worker is inside its 50ms sleep. The worker's next process_batch reads B's note_meta rows > 'M...', loads A's review-pulse.json via the pinned cdir, and INSERT OR REPLACEs B's review_schedule from the WRONG universe's review state; write_cursor pollutes B's cursor row (racing B's own worker, whose progress a crash then resumes from the polluted higher cursor, skipping the unprocessed range); when drained, finalize stamps schema_versions.review=target. From then on get_due_notes trusts is_stamped and serves B's review queue permanently missing every note <= 'M...' and carrying A-sourced schedule rows — no error anywhere, and the stamp forecloses every re-run (the module's own comment at lines 68-71: degradation here is 'baked in as built and never revisited until a repair'). For sky_backfill the same race leaves half of B's sky_nodes absent/NULL behind a completion stamp.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in source: review_backfill::run pins universe A's cdir (line 72) and cursor as thread-locals, process_batch re-locks state.db per batch with no generation/identity check (zero 'generation' matches in any *backfill*.rs), and invalidate_search_state carries no backfill-stop signal. confirmed_findings.summary: set_active_universe (async, Tokio worker) loads the registry at line 897 and holds that in-memory copy across a long body — migrate_to_constellation, nested-folder consolidation with directory moves, library-path heals — before saving it back at line 1099. Any registry mutation committed by another command inside that multi-second window (rename_universe:1194-1200, remove_universe_from_registry:1115-1120, create/open from the second window) is silently overwritten by the stale copy; both commands return Ok. switch_lock serializes only switches, not switch-vs-mutation.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: User clicks a universe to switch to it; the switch begins its consolidation/heal work (seconds on a large or network-hosted universe). While it runs, the user renames another universe in the Universe manager (sync command — completes immediately, save_registry writes the new name). The switch then reaches line 1099 and writes its registry snapshot loaded at line 897, which still carries the old name (or still carries an entry the user just removed). The rename/removal is silently reverted in universes.json with no error; the UI shows the old state again on next list_universes and nothing explains why.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in code: set_active_universe (universe.rs:858-1102, #[tauri::command(async)] → worker thread) loads the registry at line 897 with no lock and saves that same stale snapshot at line 1099; switch_lock (only usages: lines 49/56/868) serializes switch-vs-switch only. rename_universe (1194-1200) and remove_universe_from_registry (1115-1120) are sync main-thread commands doing their own unlocked load→mutate→save, so they can commit mid-switch and be silently overwritten by the line-1099 write of the line-897 snapshot — both sides return Ok, nothing is surfaced, and no reconcile heals universes.json. The window is genuinely long in the documented stalled-switch case: the §B2-5 comment states the body waits on the DB writer lock inside invalidate_search_state (line 1057, between load and save; search.rs:11228 takes state.db.lock()) and can sit behind a mid-flight backfill/reindex — the very reason the command was made async. UniverseManager.svelte::handleSwitch keeps every button enabled while awaiting the switch (no busy flag/overlay), so clicking Remove during a visibly stalled switch is a natural, reachable action; refresh() even shows the removal succeed before the stale save resurrects the entry. The same clobber silently drops a mid-window create/open registration, and a mid-switch rename (which targets the incoming universe, since active_path flips at 1042 before the 1057 stall) leaves universes.json diverged from universe.json. One correction to the candidate: rename_universe takes no id and renames only the ACTIVE universe, so "renames another universe" is imprecise — but the remove/create clobber is exact as claimed and the defect class (unlocked load → long body → last-writer-wins stale full-snapshot save) stands. Severity MED: damage is confined to registry state (membership/name/active_id) — no note content or index loss, recoverable by redoing the action — and the common-case window is ~5ms, widening to seconds only behind a backfill/reindex.

confirmed_findings.summary: migrate_legacy_data writes universe.json UNCONDITIONALLY (plain non-atomic fs::write, line 2014) and libraries.json unconditionally (fs::copy of legacy vaults.json at 1982, or `fs::write("[]").ok()` at 1985 with the I/O error swallowed), then REPLACES the whole registry with a single freshly-built entry (lines 2039-2043) without loading the existing one. The PJ-207 §15 comment on the sibling link_library_as_universe claims migrate_legacy_data 'has guarded the identical writes with !exists() all along' — true only for the four small default files (2018-2029), not for universe.json or libraries.json.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: The first-boot migration escape hatch fires (no universes.json, a legacy vaults.json present). The user picks an existing Constellation universe directory as the migration target (the folder picker allows any folder). universe.json — including the federation `children` list — is overwritten with a fresh empty manifest, and libraries.json is replaced by the legacy vaults.json content (or by "[]" with even the write error discarded by .ok()). Recipe: legacy-upgrade or reset-appdata user with an existing synced universe picks the usual parent folder and types the usual universe name — silent persisted-JSON source-of-truth loss. confirmed_findings.summary: Export-as-Note failure is console.error-only with no UI error state; a partial failure (createNote ok, writeNote fails) leaves a stub note with the composition's title as a false success cue while the composed body is lost.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: User assembles a composition in Expression Forge (drags note blocks, types transition paragraphs — user-authored text that lives only in this dialog's memory). Clicks 'Export as Note'. createNote succeeds and creates+indexes an empty stub named after the composition; writeNote of the composed body then rejects (the just-created file momentarily locked by antivirus/sync tool, or disk error). The catch at :149-151 runs console.error only — release builds have devtools disabled (feedback_devtools_dev_only), so nothing is shown anywhere; the component has no error $state and renders no failure UI. The dialog silently stays open, but the file tree now shows a note with exactly the expected title, so the user reasonably concludes the export worked and closes the forge — permanently discarding the transitions and composition order. Disk holds an empty/frontmatter-only stub; search indexes the empty stub (the reindex at :147 never runs).
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified at ExpressionForge.svelte:142-151: export is a two-step create+write. createNote → create_note (libraries.rs:1358) writes a frontmatter-only stub carrying the composition's title, indexes it synchronously (MIG-099 §3), and emits 'note-created' so the file tree shows it immediately; writeNote of the composed body then runs as a separate invoke whose rejection (transient AV/sync lock on the just-created file, disk-full after the small stub) lands in the catch at :149-151 — console.error only. The component has no error $state, no toast, and no store is set on this path; release builds disable devtools, so nothing is shown anywhere. The only behavioral difference from success is that onClose is skipped (forge stays open) — an ambiguous non-signal, actively contradicted by the strong false-success cue: a note with exactly the expected title visible in the tree AND findable in search. Closing the forge unmounts the component and permanently discards the user-authored transitions and composition order; disk and index hold an empty stub. Retry doesn't self-correct: resolve_filename_collision makes a second Export create 'Title 1.md', leaving the first stub. No guard, surfaced error, or reconcile refutes it — the write journal records the rejection but is forensic-only.

confirmed_findings.summary: The detached rename/move DB tails re-open the None window their commands closed. The 2026-08-01 fix put ensure_search_db_ready BEFORE the fs op (libraries.rs:1702, 1743, 2680), but the tails run detached AFTER the IPC settles, and a universe switch mid-tail sets state.db=None then swaps in the new universe's connection. The `if let Ok(guard)` -> `if let Some(conn)` chains at rename_item_db_tail:1854-1855, rename_folder_db_tail:1935-1936 (per-50-note chunks, so remaining chunks skip mid-loop), and move_item_db_tail:2764-2765 have no else arm and no log — the entire path-migration cascade (note_meta/review_schedule/note_aliases/note_embeddings old->new, the PJ-140 #16 earned-data preservation) silently drops. Worse, the tails load the library registry ONCE at tail start: a switch landing after that load lets the reindex loop call reindex_single_note with the OLD universe's library attribution against the NEW universe's connection, inserting foreign notes into B's note_meta/notes_fts — rows reconcile.rs never removes (its candidate predicate, lines 36-39, only touches rows under the ACTIVE universe's own accessible roots, and DriftReport.foreign_rows counts only FEDERATED roots, so a non-linked A path is counted nowhere).
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: User renames an 800-note folder in universe A (the batched tail runs for seconds), then switches to universe B before it drains. Chunks that lock after invalidate silently skip: A's index keeps every descendant at the dead pre-rename path with its review_schedule/aliases/embeddings unmigrated (gated renames suppress the watcher, so nothing heals it live); on A's next open, reconcile's cid_cn relocate is capped at max(200, 10%) rows — an 800-note folder EXCEEDS the cap, so the pass aborts and the rows stay dead. If the switch instead lands after the tail's registry load, the reindex loop writes A's notes into B's search index under A's library_name; B's search/quick-switcher then silently serve another universe's notes, and no reconcile pass on B will ever remove those rows.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in code: all three detached tails (rename_item_db_tail libraries.rs:1854-55, rename_folder_db_tail:1935-36 per-50-note chunks, move_item_db_tail:2764-65) guard with `if let Ok(guard)`/`if let Some(conn)` with no else arm, no log, and no federation-generation check, and run via spawn_blocking after the IPC settles — outside the switch_lock. set_active_universe (universe.rs:858→1057) calls invalidate_search_state, which sets *db=None (search.rs:11248); the chunked migrate loop deliberately releases the lock between batches (1945-46), so a mid-tail switch makes remaining chunks silently skip — A's index keeps every descendant at the dead pre-rename path with review_schedule/aliases/embeddings unmigrated, and gated renames suppress the watcher. Worse, the folder/move tails load the library registry ONCE at tail start (1911, 2741); after ensure_search_db_ready installs universe B's connection into the same state.db slot, the reindex loop resolves A's library names from the stale snapshot and reindex_single_note (search.rs:12682) → index_note_impl (7884, only gate is path.exists(), true since A's files remain on disk) fully indexes A's notes into B's note_meta/notes_fts. Reconcile structurally never heals B: removal candidates must sit under an accessible OWN root (reconcile.rs:36-39) and foreign_rows counts only FEDERATED roots (98-107) — an unlinked A is counted nowhere; the module's own doc documents 603 such out-of-root rows persisting. The relocate cap max(200,10%) (56-59) aborts on an 800-row set for a ≤8,000-note universe, confirming the A-side arithmetic. Partial mitigation: the PJ-207 drift notice surfaces the A-side dead rows on A's next open (delayed-visible, not permanently silent), and the single-note tail re-resolves libraries post-switch so its foreign-insert leg is guarded — but the B-side contamination from folder/move tails is fully silent, served by B's search/quick-switcher, and permanent with no removal path. rename_item_db_tail even logs "reindex OK" when the reindex no-opped on a None db (false-success log).

The RMW is also outside gate_rmw/any lock, and both are sync commands doing disk I/O on the IPC dispatch thread.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: User clicks a column header to re-sort a base (update_base_order): the file is truncated, then the new YAML is written. App crash, power loss, or an AV/sync-tool sharing violation between the truncate and the flush leaves the .base zero-length or partial on disk. No error surfaces (the command never returned). Next open, parse_lens_yaml fails on the truncated file — the user's entire lens definition (scope, filters, columns, order) is gone, with nothing to recover from: no temp file, no net, no journal entry. confirmed_findings.reason: Verified by direct read: update_base_columns (src-tauri/src/lens/query.rs:393) and update_base_order (query.rs:421) rewrite an EXISTING user-authored .base file with bare std::fs::write — truncate-then-write, no temp/rename/fsync — as do convert_base's in-place legacy upgrade (src-tauri/src/bases.rs:312) and save_workspace_base (bases.rs:780). A crash, power loss, or AV/sync sharing-violation between truncate and flush leaves the .base zero-length or partial; the command never returns so no error surfaces, and next open parse_lens_yaml fails with the lens definition (scope, filters, columns, order) unrecoverable — no journal, backup, or .trash covers .base files, and unlike update_note_property these commands sit outside gate_rmw. This is the exact defect class the codebase itself has confirmed and fixed four times via crate::universe::atomic_write (canvas.rs:79 PJ-207 §15, link_types.rs:547 2026-08-02 triage, style_presets.rs:49, review.rs:907, libraries.rs:480 G6/PJ-140) — these base writers were missed in those sweeps. Refutation attempts failed: error handling only covers returned Err, not the crash window; no lock/guard/recovery exists; the handlers are live BaseTab gestures. bases.rs:362/744 are new-file creations (exists() guard) and carry no pre-existing content risk. Fix: route the four existing-file writers through atomic_write, matching canvas.rs:96.

confirmed_findings.summary: The folder trash-fallback's copy+remove serializes only on the FOLDER's path lock; a debounced editor save to a note INSIDE the folder locks a different key, so a save landing between copy and remove_dir_all is deleted while the surviving .trash copy keeps pre-save content.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: move_into_trash_folder's cross-device/persistent-sharing-violation fallback wraps copy_dir_recursive + fs::remove_dir_all in with_path_lock(source) — the FOLDER path. The Batch-2 comment ('a save landing between the copy and the remove used to be silently lost… now it serializes') is only true for a FILE source: write_gate locks are exact-path keyed (lock_key, write_gate.rs:131), so an editor's debounced gate_write to `<folder>/note.md` takes a DIFFERENT lock and does not serialize against the folder's fallback. Recipe: a note inside the folder is open with unsaved edits; the user deletes the folder to .trash; gate_rename fails non-collision after its 5 retries (AV/indexer holding a descendant — the fallback's designed trigger) → fallback copies note.md (old bytes) → the ≥1.5 s debounced save fires and gate_write lands the new bytes into the doomed source → remove_dir_all deletes them. The trash copy — the only surviving copy of a note the user may later restore — silently lacks the final edits; delete_path returns Ok, the write journal shows a successful gated write, and nothing records that the written bytes never reached the trash.
confirmed_findings.reason: Mechanism verified in code: write_gate lock keys are exact-path (write_gate.rs:131-141, no prefix locking), so with_path_lock(source) on the FOLDER (libraries.rs:8607) does not serialize a gate_write to a descendant note — the Batch-2 comment's "now it serializes" holds only for the file branch, exactly as claimed. The fallback is reachable (trash_move_decolliding returns NotRenamed on any non-collision gate_rename failure; a Windows directory rename fails while AV/indexer holds a descendant handle through the 5 retries). However, the candidate's stated recipe is partially defused by a guard it did not examine: both live callers of delete_path (deleteWithSetting store.ts:5099, moveToTrash store.ts:5282) await preserveWorkBeforeVacating first, which since 2026-08-03 flushes every dirty open note AT-OR-UNDER the folder to disk before the backend delete — so pre-click unsaved edits DO reach the trash copy, and a failed flush keeps the write-ahead net with a visible banner. What survives is narrower: the tab stays open and editable until deletePath resolves (releaseTabsForVacatedPath runs after the await, store.ts:5112), so keystrokes typed during the in-flight fallback delete (~750ms rename retries + multi-second copy_dir_recursive) can debounce-save into the doomed source between that file's copy and remove_dir_all — gate_write succeeds under the uncontested descendant lock, journals ok, remove_dir_all deletes the bytes, preserved=true then wipes the recovery state, and the .trash copy (the advertised recoverable version) silently lacks the final edits with no surfaced error. On the primary rename path the same late save fails loudly (parent gone → surfaced save failure), so the silence is fallback-specific. Real, silent, reachable — but multi-condition and bounded to edits typed within the seconds-long delete window of a folder the user just deleted: LOW stands.

confirmed_findings.summary: A retyped note title is committed ONLY by the input's blur handler (handleTitleBlur:1177 → ontitlechange); onDestroy (1030-1046) flushes the body but never commits a pending title edit, and destroying a focused input fires no blur — so any teardown that is not preceded by a real blur silently discards the typed rename. FocusPane has the identical hole (FocusPane.svelte:322 onDestroy commits body only; PJ-187 fixed only the Escape path).
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: User clicks into the title, types the new name, and without pressing Enter or clicking away: (a) switches tabs with a keyboard shortcut — the {#key tab.id|path} teardown destroys the focused input with no blur event; or (b) an external/watcher change to the SAME note arrives — adoptExternalChangeIntoTabs adopts (the model is clean: title typing never dirties the model) and bumps reloadVersion, remounting NotePane mid-edit. In both cases the typed title vanishes and the old title re-renders, with no error, no journal entry, and no cue that a rename was ever attempted. The user's rename intent (and in the watcher case possibly minutes-old typing in the title field) is silently lost.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in source: ontitlechange fires ONLY from handleTitleBlur (NotePane.svelte:1177, wired to onblur at :1692; Enter commits only via view.focus()-induced blur), and onDestroy (:1030-1046) flushes the body (doFlush) but never commits a pending title. Removing a focused element fires no blur (WHATWG focus-fixup rule; Chromium/WebView2). A concrete keyboard-only recipe is reachable: handleGlobalKeydown (+layout.svelte:4672-4676) passes modifier combos through even when the title input is focused, and defaults Ctrl+E (toggle-edit), Ctrl+W (close-note), Alt+ArrowLeft (nav-back) each tear down NotePane via the {#key} block (NoteEditor.svelte:773) with no blur — the typed title silently reverts with no error, journal entry, or cue. The watcher path also holds: title typing mutates only local titleValue (model stays clean), so adoptExternalChangeIntoTabs (store.ts:1347-1371) adopts and bumps reloadVersion, remounting NotePane mid-title-edit and discarding the in-flight title. FocusPane has the identical hole (onDestroy:322-332 = flushNow body only; PJ-187 covered only Escape). Severity stays LOW: all mouse-driven departures (clicking a tab, tree, or anywhere) move focus and fire blur before teardown, so the common paths self-heal; the loss is uncommitted in-flight input (a rename intent), never a persisted title, file content, or index state.

confirmed_findings.summary: The workspace save's second-screen state request falls back to tabs: [] on a 2s timeout, silently persisting an EMPTY second-screen tab list into workspaces.json ('the precious file' — store.ts:7632, no .prev rotation) whenever the SS webview is busy past 2s, overwriting whatever SS arrangement the workspace previously held.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: The user saves a named workspace while the second screen is mid-loadAllData on the 7,820-note universe (or mid-LocalSkyView layout) and the screen:state-response misses the 2s window. The catch at :10077-10080 writes secondScreen = { open: true, tabs: [], activeTabPath: null } into the named workspace with no error surfaced — the previously-saved SS tab arrangement in that workspace is gone. Currently damped because onRestore (:10102-10107) deliberately never restores SS state (SS always starts closed), so the corrupted record is write-only today — but any future restore of that field replays the silent loss.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified end-to-end: the 2s timeout catch at +layout.svelte:10077-10080 silently substitutes tabs:[] for the second screen's real state and WorkspaceManager.handleSave → saveWorkspace (store.ts:7710-7736) durably persists it into workspaces.json — the no-.prev-rotation "precious file" — with same-name saves replacing the prior record, and no error surfaced on any hop (empty catch, handleSave reports nothing, persistWorkspaces only errors on IPC failure). Reachable: the SS responder (SecondScreenPage.svelte:820, u6) is an in-webview handler registered late in an awaited onMount chain; a webview blocked >2s mid-loadAllData on the 7,820-note universe, or still mid-onMount, misses the window. Severity capped at LOW because the secondScreen field is verifiably write-only today: onRestore (+layout.svelte:10084-10108) ignores it and force-closes the SS, and sendWorkspaceRestore is imported but never called anywhere in src/, so the SS-side onWorkspaceRestore (u7) never fires — the corrupted record has no consumer until SS restore is wired, at which point every timeout-tainted save replays as silent arrangement loss.

confirmed_findings.summary: review_schedule.stratum is maintained only when the note ITSELF is re-indexed (upsert_schedule_row reads sky_nodes.stratum at search.rs:8321-8328, before that save's own link writes land), while a neighbour's link edit updates sky_nodes.stratum via maintain_sky_after_save but never touches the target's review_schedule row. The in-code heal claim — 'a stratum gone stale via a neighbour's link edit ... self-heals on the periodic reconcile' — names a pass that is not periodic: review::recompute_all_in is invoked only from converge.rs:324, i.e. the marker-armed crash heal or a user-run index repair.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Note B accumulates inbound links from other notes' saves over weeks without being edited itself. sky_nodes.stratum for B rises write-time (maintain_sky_after_save), but review_schedule.stratum for B stays at the value captured at B's last save. get_due_notes sorts 'higher stratum first' (review.rs:493-496) and the Reviewer displays the row's stratum, so B is silently mis-ranked in the due queue and shown with a stale stratum indefinitely — no error, no drift detector (the drift check stats .md files and is structurally blind to a derived table disagreeing with another derived table), and no heal until the user happens to save B or runs a full repair.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in code: maintain_sky_after_save (search.rs:2706-2726) updates only sky_nodes.stratum for link-affected neighbours; review_schedule.stratum is written solely by upsert_schedule_row from index_note (search.rs:8321-8328) when the note ITSELF is re-indexed, plus the backfill/repair paths. Stratum genuinely depends on inbound links (stratum_sql_expr's ≥5-inbound and distinct-source signals, search.rs:188-218), so a note accumulating inbound links without being edited gets a rising sky_nodes.stratum and a frozen review_schedule.stratum. The in-code heal claim ("periodic reconcile", review.rs:1392-1393) is doc drift: recompute_all_in is reachable only via converge Families::All, whose two entry points are after_repair_run (user-triggered index repair, index_repair.rs:897 → search.rs:12111) and heal_interrupted_walk (derived_heal.rs:215, crash-marker-armed only) — nothing periodic. get_due_notes reads and sorts by the stale rs.stratum (review.rs:235/310/496) with no surfaced error, and the drift detector is structurally blind to derived-vs-derived disagreement (converge.rs:409-411). Severity stays LOW: no source-of-truth loss — the consequence is a silently mis-ranked due queue and a stale displayed stratum, healed on the note's own next save, any repair run, or crash heal, and diluted by the frontend's effective-priority re-sort.

confirmed_findings.summary: quoteIfNeeded escapes embedded double-quotes but NOT backslashes before wrapping the value in a YAML double-quoted scalar, so any value containing both a backslash and a quote-trigger character (`:`, `#`, `[`, leading `-`, etc.) is emitted as an invalid or wrongly-decoded scalar: `\U`/`\d`-style sequences are invalid YAML escapes (the whole frontmatter becomes unparseable → every later property write H1-refused), and `\n`/`\t` silently decode to control characters on the next read. Reaches disk via the two callers PJ-187 wired: rebrandCopyFrontmatter's recovery-copy retitle (store.ts:552) and the template-create canonical-field merge (+layout.svelte:4802). reconstructFrontmatter's inline scalar quoter (store.ts:2885) has the same missing backslash escape but only feeds the tab.content cache.

confirmed_findings.summary: Renaming a property key by clearing the field first durably DELETES the property from the .md mid-rename: updateKey fires debouncedSave on every keystroke, an empty key makes the row non-committable (propsCommit.ts:41), and plan (propsCommit.ts:103) derives removal from 'seeded key absent from local rows' — indistinguishable from a deliberate delete. The 800 ms commit removes the key (and its whole list) from model and disk; it is re-added only when the user finishes typing the new name. Slow typing also commits every intermediate key prefix ('s', 'st', 'sta'…) to disk, each with a full write + reindex.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: User selects the `related:` key (12 wikilink items), presses Backspace to clear it, and pauses more than 800 ms composing the new name — the debounce fires a remove op and the list is spliced out of the .md and the index. The app then crashes, the laptop sleeps, or the user is interrupted and closes the app: the 12 links are durably gone with no error, no trash entry, and no banner — the panel showed a blank-keyed row still holding the values, but the disk never got them back.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified end-to-end in code: the key field's oninput (PropertyEditor.svelte:1164) routes every keystroke through updateKey → debouncedSave (800 ms → commitAndSave). A cleared key makes the row non-committable (propsCommit.ts:41), touchedSince marks the vanished seeded key as deleted (propsCommit.ts:183-185), and plan emits {op:'remove'} (propsCommit.ts:102-104) — the rename path never uses the atomic renamePropKeyIn intent. commitAndSave applies the remove to the model and saveTabContent durably writes the .md without the property; seededRows is then re-seeded from the model (line 1051), so the blank-keyed row holding the values survives only in the panel. Any ordinary interruption completes the loss silently: crash/sleep; an in-place wikilink navigation, whose PJ-187 guard DROPS the pending rows by design (console.warn only, devtools dev-only in release); or tab/app close, whose onDestroy flush filters the blank row as non-committable. No banner, no trash entry, no undo surface for a removed frontmatter key. The secondary claim also holds: >800 ms pauses while typing the new name commit each intermediate prefix as remove+add pairs with full compose+write+reindex. Refutation fails: no guard defers the save while the key is blank, the write succeeds (so nothing lands in the refused/banner path), and completion-self-heal only applies if the rename is finished. Severity stays LOW: single property per incident, narrow pause-plus-interruption window, self-heals on normal completion.

confirmed_findings.summary: resolve_structural_conflict's reindex tail discards the reindex result: `let _ = crate::search::reindex_single_note(...)`. The sibling rename tail (lines 1880-1883) logs both the Ok and Err arms to the diagnostics log; here only the no-own-library skip arm (2642-2645) is logged — a reindex that RUNS and FAILS leaves no trace anywhere.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: User resolves a structural parent/contains conflict; gate_rmw rewrites the note's frontmatter on disk successfully. reindex_single_note then fails (writer-lock contention timeout, transient SQLITE_BUSY). The error is discarded: note_meta/notes_fts keep the pre-rewrite frontmatter for this note — structure panel, search and backlinks serve stale data while the file on disk says otherwise — with no log line distinguishing this from a clean run, until some unrelated save or the next boot reconcile happens to touch the note.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in source: resolve_structural_conflict (libraries.rs:2641) discards reindex_single_note's Result with `let _ =` after gate_rmw has already durably rewritten the note's frontmatter on disk. reindex_single_note (search.rs:12682) does not log its own failures — a poisoned db-lock (12688) or an index_note error (12718 `?`: transient file-read I/O such as a Windows AV lock on the just-written .md, or a SQLite write error) propagates to the caller and is dropped. The command then returns Ok(()) and emits cascade:rewrote, so the frontend shows full success and the reloaded tab looks correct while note_meta/notes_fts keep the pre-resolve frontmatter — a real index↔disk divergence with no log line, indistinguishable from a clean run. The site violates the codebase's own PJ-254 convention: the sibling rename tail (1880–1888) logs BOTH the Ok and Err arms, and this site's comment ("a skipped reindex is logged, never silent") is honored only for the no-own-library skip arm (2642–2645). The watcher cannot self-correct it (suppressed on this write path per the 2597–2605 doc comment). Severity stays LOW because the disk source of truth is intact and the divergence window is bounded: PJ-207's reconcile compares file mtime vs note_meta.modified and would flag the note as drifted at the next scan, and any later successful save of the note repairs it. Fix is one line: use the rename tail's match-and-diag_log shape.

confirmed_findings.summary: libraries.json mutators are unserialized read-modify-writes: retarget_registered_libraries (612), add_library (815), remove_library (876), bring_in_library all do try_load_libraries → mutate Vec → save_libraries with no registry-wide lock. save_libraries (476) is atomic per-write but the RMW cycle is not. rename_item (1672) and move_item (2658) are #[tauri::command(async)] — they run concurrently on tokio worker threads — and both call retarget_registered_libraries inside the command body, so two overlapping folder ops (or a folder op overlapping an add/remove) interleave load→save and the last writer silently reverts the other's registry change.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: A folder rename that carries a nested registered library (retarget rewrites its path in libraries.json) runs concurrently with a second registry mutation — e.g. a drag-drop move_item retargeting another library, or an add_library from the sidebar. Both load the same registry snapshot; writer 2 saves last and re-persists the library at its OLD pre-rename path. No error anywhere (both commands returned Ok). The registration now points at a dead directory: the sidebar tree, every walker, the indexer and the boot reconcile treat the library's real notes as unowned (reconcile counts them as foreign_rows and skips them) — the library and its notes silently vanish from every surface on next boot.
confirmed_findings.reason: The unserialized read-modify-write is real and code-verified: retarget_registered_libraries (619→661), add_library (828→853), remove_library (877→885), and set_library_canonical_mode all do try_load_libraries → mutate → save_libraries with no lock spanning the cycle; save_libraries is atomic per-write only. Concurrency is real: rename_item (1672), move_item (2658), delete_path (8460), and bring_in_library (mig108.rs:2332) are all #[tauri::command(async)] on worker threads, and bring_in_library calls add_library's RMW on a worker thread too. The write_gate is per-path only (write_gate.rs:117) and LIBRARIES_CACHE guards only the cache — no registry-wide lock exists. The lost update is silent (both commands return Ok) and deceptive (retarget logs 'carried library X → new path' before the other writer reverts it), and the code's own comments confirm no self-heal for a dead registry path. However, severity is capped below MED: every mutator is a discrete human gesture, the frontend already serializes the realistic pairs (batch move is a sequential await loop at +layout.svelte:6988; renames are guarded by renamesInFlight; add/remove/bring-in are single awaited modal-dialog invokes), the interleave window is only the ms-scale load→save span, and the candidate's blast radius is overstated — under MIG-108 the notes fall to the universe_notes root library by longest-root-wins, staying indexed and visible as an ordinary folder; only the library's registration/identity is lost, and re-adding the library at its new path recovers it with no note content touched.

confirmed_findings.summary: The path→baseYaml disk read has a re-entry guard (loadedPath) but no stale-RESULT guard: `invoke('read_note',{filePath:path}).then(txt => { baseYaml = txt })` commits whichever response resolves last. Every sibling async effect in the codebase (BaseTab's own lens-eval effect at line 95 uses lastRun; ReviewStatusPanel uses gen; Inspector360 uses seq) discards out-of-order results — this one doesn't. baseYaml then drives BOTH the rendered lens AND the column/order write-back path (updateBaseColumns/updateBaseOrder at lines 136/173 persist UI state derived from the displayed definition to `path`).
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: The `path` prop changes from base A to base B while A's read_note is still in flight (slow/AV-scanned disk). B's read resolves first, A's resolves last → baseYaml holds A's YAML while path = B. The pane silently renders base A's definition under base B's tab. The user then adjusts columns or clicks a sort header: update_base_columns(path=B, columns derived from A's displayed definition) re-reads B from disk and persists A's column set into B's .base file — returning Ok and re-rendering as success. B's real column configuration is silently overwritten with another base's.
confirmed_findings.reason: All four links verified in code. (1) BaseTab.svelte:87-89 commits the read_note result with no stale-result guard, while the adjacent lens-eval effect (line 106) and every sibling async effect uses one — the pattern was known and omitted here. (2) +layout.svelte:9245 mounts BaseTab with no {#key}, so switching between two open .base tabs updates `path` on the live instance; the effect issues read(B) while read(A) can still be in flight, and if A resolves last, baseYaml holds A's YAML with path=B. (3) The `path === loadedPath` re-entry guard then prevents any re-read, so base A's definition renders under base B's tab permanently — no error surfaced. (4) A subsequent column add/remove/reorder or sort-header click calls update_base_columns/update_base_order (query.rs:363/405) with path=B and columns/order derived from A's displayed definition; the command reads B from disk, swaps in A's column list (which validates, since the dims are registered), writes B, and returns Ok — B's real column/sort configuration is silently overwritten and the UI re-renders as success. Mitigations that cap severity: tiny race window (two near-simultaneous reads of small YAML files, earlier read must out-lose the later), requires a follow-up write gesture during the misrender, the wrong lens_name is visible in the header, split view is immune (keyed per tab.id), and the loss is view config (columns/order; scope/where preserved), not note content — recoverable by reconfiguring. Fix: guard the .then with a captured request token, exactly as the lens-eval effect below it already does.
